To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ET kinetics of TTF/TTF˙+ and TCNQ/ TCNQ˙- in acetonitrilic solution at conventional electrodes (Pt, Au and GC) are fast and close the reversible limit and are in good agreement for both FTACV and SECM measurements, whereas at pBDD the kinetics vary across the surface, and the availability of charge carriers, which decreases at more negative potentials, results in lower apparent k values and unusual voltammetric wavess

the apparent charge transfer kinetic parameters determined by FTAC and SECM for the one-electron ET processes studied at Pt, Au, GC and pBDD electrodes in acetonitrilic solution are consistent with those determined by SECM, which are in good agreement, but that the apparent charge-transfer parameters at pBDD are influenced by the complex heterogeneous surface structure, the degenerate p-type surface doping and the lower availability of charge carriers compared to conventional electrodes.

the apparent heterogeneous ET rate constants for the oxidation of TTF and reduction of TCNQ in acetonitrilic solution are fast and close the reversible limit at conventional Pt, Au, GC and pBDD electrodes, with the latter exhibiting a distribution of k values across its surface.

the measurement of heterogeneous charge transfer kinetic data is dependent on the measurement technique and electrode material.

the choice of measurement technique and electrode material is critical for determining the apparent charge transfer kinetics of redox reactions, and this is particularly important when using diamond electrodes.
